# helmsman-tests

Procedure once a test or an end-to-end file is open. Test choice selects watchable end-to-end, integration, or pure unit. The three end-to-end facts, the protected-test rule, and which layer counts live in `helmsman-standards.mdc`. If `.helmsman/setup.md` is present, it names the Helmsman runner. If it is absent, use the repo's native journey: `pnpm test:e2e`, Playwright, Cypress, Maestro, or the pull-request smoke. Do not stop to create that file, and do not start helmsman-setup.

## E2E smoke

The suite a person can watch. One journey per test. Cover the success path and the error the UI shows. Each journey opens its own start URL.

Wait on a condition you can see, or a named network call. Never a fixed sleep (`cy.wait(ms)`, `page.waitForTimeout`, a Maestro sleep used as the readiness check).

Selectors: a stable test id, or the role and name a person sees. Not a generated id, a hashed class, or placeholder text. Name test ids `{feature}-{element}-{type}`.

If a click cannot fire the control, fix the control. Do not force a click on a non-interactive node as the lasting fix.

Cache sign-in only with a check that the session is still live. Use the runner the repo already runs. A Helmsman `Watch` or `E2E smoke` line is that runner only when a full install records it. Do not add a second runner.

## pass

An integration shows code and infrastructure working together, against a real local database, queue, or emulator. Raise one when a change can pass the unit test and the e2e smoke and still be wrong at that boundary. Do not mock that boundary inside the integration.

## Unit test

A unit test is a pure function only. Cover it completely, including empty input and the edge. Mock nothing. There is no boundary to mock.

## Pins

Do not add an assertion to a green test, rewrite a green journey, weaken an assertion, widen a tolerance, skip a case, or delete a case to get green. The test diff mostly adds cases. If most of a hunk sits inside an old test, stop and split.

```typescript
// BAD — new case stuffed into the old test
expect(tax(100, 0.2)).toBe(20);
expect(tax(100, 0)).toBe(0);

// GOOD — old test untouched; new behavior is a new test
it("returns zero when the rate is zero", () => {
  expect(tax(100, 0)).toBe(0);
});
```
